declared_purpose: Generate configurable tech-news digests from six source layers, score and deduplicate articles, and produce formatted reports for configured delivery and archival. Email and full-text enrichment are conditional. The digest workflow explicitly requires source links, KOL metrics, all qualifying releases, and 90-day archive retention; authentication, caching, subprocess environment sharing, and diagnostics are implementation choices. Basis: SKILL.md:2-3; references/digest-prompt.md:67-118,127-148.

data_operations.operation: Read and merge local configuration
data_operations.source: Default sources/topics and optional workspace overlays
data_operations.data_scope: Feed URLs, monitored handles, repositories, subreddits, topic queries, priorities, filters, and display preferences
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local configuration loader and calling components
data_operations.condition: Configuration is loaded for the selected component; matching user entries override defaults.

data_operations.operation: Fetch RSS content and select article metadata
data_operations.source: Enabled configured RSS/Atom feeds
data_operations.data_scope: Requests disclose the configured URL, User-Agent, and applicable cache validators. Responses are read in full; output articles retain titles, links, dates, and configured topics, generally capped at 20 per feed.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Configured feed servers; local fetch results
data_operations.condition: RSS fetching runs unless skipped or reusable output is accepted; retry and time-window filters apply.

data_operations.operation: Resolve accounts and fetch posts through official X API
data_operations.source: Configured Twitter handles and X_BEARER_TOKEN
data_operations.data_scope: Discloses handles or resolved user IDs and bearer authentication. Requests tweet dates, metrics, context annotations, references, author expansion, and user verification/metrics; locally retains filtered post text, URLs, dates, metrics, IDs, and topics.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: api.x.com/2; local official-backend results
data_operations.condition: Official backend is explicitly selected or selected by auto detection when higher-priority credentials are absent. Account lookup uses valid cached IDs where available.

data_operations.operation: Fetch posts through twitterapi.io
data_operations.source: Configured handles and TWITTERAPI_IO_KEY
data_operations.data_scope: Discloses handle, reply-exclusion flag, pagination cursor when used, and API-key authentication; receives posts and retains text, links, timestamps, post IDs, and engagement metrics.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: api.twitterapi.io/twitter/user/last_tweets; local backend results
data_operations.condition: twitterapiio backend is selected; a second page is conditionally fetched and errors may cause retries.

data_operations.operation: Fetch posts through GetXAPI
data_operations.source: Configured handles and GETX_API_KEY
data_operations.data_scope: Discloses handle, conditional pagination cursor, and bearer API-key authentication; retains filtered post text, links, dates, IDs, and engagement metrics.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: api.getxapi.com/twitter/user/tweets; local backend results
data_operations.condition: getxapi is selected explicitly, or first in auto mode when GETX_API_KEY is present. Page-two fetching and retries are conditional.

data_operations.operation: Resolve GitHub authentication locally
data_operations.source: GITHUB_TOKEN; GH_APP_ID, GH_APP_INSTALL_ID, GH_APP_KEY_FILE; gh auth token
data_operations.data_scope: Environment credentials and settings, key-file existence, or a token returned by gh. Logs include credential presence/type rather than token values.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Calling GitHub component; gh subprocess on the fallback path
data_operations.condition: Each GitHub command resolves authentication: environment token, then configured App credentials, then gh, then unauthenticated access. Resolution also occurs when the release source list is empty.

data_operations.operation: Read, temporarily duplicate, use, and delete a private key
data_operations.source: Private-key PEM file identified by GH_APP_KEY_FILE
data_operations.data_scope: Entire private key is read into Python memory and copied to a temporary PEM file; openssl signs a constructed JWT. The temporary copy is unlinked in finally.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Python process memory, temporary filesystem file, and local openssl subprocess
data_operations.condition: GitHub App authentication is attempted after GITHUB_TOKEN is absent and all required App settings and key file exist.

data_operations.operation: Exchange a signed JWT for an installation token
data_operations.source: Locally constructed and signed GitHub App JWT
data_operations.data_scope: App identifier in JWT, installation identifier in request path, signed bearer JWT; receives an installation token. The private key itself is not included in this request.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: api.github.com/app/installations/{install_id}/access_tokens; returned token stays with the calling component
data_operations.condition: GitHub App token generation reaches the exchange step.

data_operations.operation: Fetch GitHub releases
data_operations.source: Enabled repository configuration and resolved optional GitHub token
data_operations.data_scope: Discloses repository identity, optional bearer authentication, and conditional cache validators. Reads release responses; retains recent non-draft release titles, URLs, dates, and shortened release summaries.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: api.github.com/repos/{repo}/releases; local release-result JSON
data_operations.condition: Release fetching runs for enabled repositories; retries, time filtering, and a 20-release processing cap apply.

data_operations.operation: Search repositories and infer a growth estimate
data_operations.source: Four built-in GitHub queries, repository metadata, and optional authentication
data_operations.data_scope: Discloses topic queries, push-date cutoff, star threshold, result count, and optional token. Retains repository identity, description, stars, forks, language, dates, and topics. daily_stars_est is inferred from total stars divided by repository age, rather than measured daily growth.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: api.github.com/search/repositories; local trending JSON
data_operations.condition: Trending command runs; it uses built-in queries independently of workspace source overlays.

data_operations.operation: Fetch and filter Reddit listings
data_operations.source: Enabled subreddit configuration
data_operations.data_scope: Discloses subreddit, sort, listing limit, and request headers without API authentication. Reads listing responses; retains selected titles, URLs, dates, flair, post type, scores, comment counts, upvote ratios, and topics.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: www.reddit.com/r/{subreddit}/{sort}.json; local Reddit results
data_operations.condition: Reddit fetching runs; local time, score, and pinned-post filters apply.

data_operations.operation: Search with Brave
data_operations.source: Configured topic queries and BRAVE_API_KEYS or BRAVE_API_KEY
data_operations.data_scope: Discloses query, freshness, language/country/safety settings, result count, User-Agent, and subscription token. Receives titles, URLs, and snippets; errors may repeat the query using another configured key.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: api.search.brave.com/res/v1/web/search; local filtered search results
data_operations.condition: Brave is explicitly selected with keys, or auto mode selects it after Tavily is unavailable.

data_operations.operation: Search with Tavily
data_operations.source: Configured topic queries and TAVILY_API_KEY
data_operations.data_scope: POST body contains API key, query, search depth, news topic, result count, answer-disable flag, and optional day limit. Results retain titles, URLs, dates, and snippets truncated to 300 characters.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: api.tavily.com/search; local filtered search results
data_operations.condition: Tavily is explicitly selected with a key or preferred by auto mode.

data_operations.operation: Probe Brave account limits
data_operations.source: Configured Brave keys
data_operations.data_scope: Sends a synthetic test query and authentication; reads rate-limit and remaining-quota headers to derive concurrency and exhaustion state.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Brave search endpoint; local rate-limit cache keyed by positional key labels, without storing key values
data_operations.condition: A candidate key lacks usable fresh cache state and BRAVE_PLAN does not bypass probing; exhausted/error keys may cause further probes.

data_operations.operation: Persist and reuse local fetch caches
data_operations.source: RSS/GitHub response validators, official X account lookup results, and Brave probe results
data_operations.data_scope: Feed/API URLs with ETag, Last-Modified and timestamps; handle-to-user-ID mappings with timestamps; Brave quota/concurrency state. Valid RSS/GitHub validators are subsequently returned to their corresponding request endpoints.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: /tmp/tech-news-digest-rss-cache.json; /tmp/tech-news-digest-github-cache.json; /tmp/tech-news-digest-twitter-id-cache.json; /tmp/tech-news-digest-brave-rate-limit.json
data_operations.condition: Cache loading and reuse depend on component flags and freshness. RSS/GitHub validators use 24-hour freshness; official X IDs use seven days; Brave state uses 24 hours. Freshness checks do not globally delete expired records.

data_operations.operation: Run local subprocesses and stage pipeline data
data_operations.source: Parent environment, fetch outputs, and subprocess stdout/stderr
data_operations.data_scope: Every step inherits the entire environment. Fetch results are staged as JSON; the parent reads output statistics, captures process output, and persists timing/count/status metadata plus error tails on failures.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local fetch, merge, and enrichment subprocesses; td-pipeline-* run directory; final output and adjacent .meta.json; optional output-stem-debug directory
data_operations.condition: Default pipeline runs six fetch steps; skip/only/reuse options alter execution. Successful runs remove generated run directories unless reused. Merge failure returns before cleanup; --debug copies intermediates for retention.

data_operations.operation: Read prior reports and derive ranked, deduplicated article records
data_operations.source: Fetch-result JSON and Markdown archive files
data_operations.data_scope: Reads full source JSON and eligible archive files; extracts prior titles, derives quality scores, repeat flags, multi-source indicators, and primary topics. Duplicate/domain-limited records are omitted from merged output.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local merge component and merged JSON, normally /tmp/td-merged.json
data_operations.condition: Merge runs after collection. Archive-title lookup defaults to 14 days using dates in filenames; undated filenames are not excluded by that date test. The agent separately reads the latest full report for repeats and developing stories.

data_operations.operation: Conditionally fetch and persist article text
data_operations.source: Article links selected from merged JSON
data_operations.data_scope: Sends the original article URL with Markdown/HTML Accept and User-Agent headers. Reads the full response, extracts text, and retains up to 2,000 characters by default with method/token metadata.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Selected article URL's server, possibly served through Cloudflare; enriched local JSON, overwriting input by default
data_operations.condition: Pipeline --enrich is enabled, or the script is invoked directly. Defaults select up to 15 eligible URLs, normally score at least 10 or whitelisted blogs at least 3; skip-listed domains are not requested. The Cloudflare path is content negotiation at the article URL, not a separate upload API.

data_operations.operation: Return a selected article overview to the caller
data_operations.source: Merged JSON
data_operations.data_scope: Prints counts, topics, top-ranked titles, source names, links, shortened snippets, engagement metrics, and Reddit scores/comments.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local stdout and the invoking agent/tool caller; no additional remote recipient is specified
data_operations.condition: Digest workflow invokes summarize-merged.py with a per-topic limit; optional topic filtering is available.

data_operations.operation: Archive reports and delete old archives
data_operations.source: Generated digest Markdown
data_operations.data_scope: Selected news, summaries, attribution, links, scores, engagement statistics, report date, and source-count footer
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: <WORKSPACE>/archive/tech-news-digest/<MODE>-YYYY-MM-DD.md
data_operations.condition: The prompt explicitly directs saving each report and deleting files older than 90 days. This is an agent instruction; packaged Python does not implement the archive-deletion step.

data_operations.operation: Convert reports into local HTML and PDF artifacts
data_operations.source: Digest Markdown or agent-generated email HTML
data_operations.data_scope: Report content is converted to escaped HTML or passed as generated HTML to weasyprint; verbose PDF generation also saves an HTML copy.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Specified HTML/PDF output files, normally /tmp/td-email.html and /tmp/td-digest.pdf; verbose PDF sidecar .html
data_operations.condition: Formatting scripts are invoked; scheduled email workflow requires a PDF attempt and permits omission if generation fails.

data_operations.operation: Disclose the finished report through chat delivery
data_operations.source: Generated digest
data_operations.data_scope: Selected news summaries, source links, public-author attribution, required KOL metrics, scores, and footer statistics
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: message tool targeting DISCORD_CHANNEL_ID; alternatively a configured user ID for DM delivery
data_operations.condition: The configured Discord delivery path is followed; the PDF template separately describes optional attachment delivery.

data_operations.operation: Build and hand off email for delivery
data_operations.source: Recipient/sender placeholders, static subject, local HTML, and optional PDF
data_operations.data_scope: Reads full HTML and attachment bytes; constructs MIME containing subject, From, To, local-time Date, body, and attachment filename/content. Recipient addresses, subject, attachment path, and transport errors can appear in local logs.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local msmtp subprocess, then sendmail fallback; configured EMAIL recipients through externally configured mail transport
data_operations.condition: EMAIL is set. Main workflow requires the same items as Discord and attempts a PDF attachment. Transport failure triggers fallback; no artifact deletion is shown.

data_operations.operation: Describe alternative email handoffs
data_operations.source: Email and PDF template examples
data_operations.data_scope: Email template passes recipient, subject, and HTML to gog gmail send; PDF template passes an attachment and recipient to mail.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local gog or mail CLI and configured email recipient; underlying transport is unspecified
data_operations.condition: An agent follows these template-specific examples. These differ from the main workflow's send-email.py route and are not subprocess calls made by that Python script.

data_operations.operation: Persist source-health history and infer failure rates
data_operations.source: Explicitly supplied fetch-result JSON and prior health state
data_operations.data_scope: Retains source IDs/names and timestamped success flags; derives failure fractions and logs unhealthy source names.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: /tmp/tech-news-digest-source-health.json and local logging
data_operations.condition: source-health.py is invoked separately; the unified pipeline does not invoke it. Checks are pruned to seven days only for sources present in the current update.

data_operations.operation: Package historical test data and read it in local unit tests
data_operations.source: Captured RSS, Twitter, GitHub, Reddit, web, and merged fixtures
data_operations.data_scope: Public article/post content and URLs, public account identities, engagement metrics, timestamps, query records, and processing metadata. Fixture configuration paths are redacted; GitHub authentication is represented by a boolean.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Packaged tests/fixtures/*.json and local test processes; configuration tests also create temporary synthetic overlays
data_operations.condition: Fixture persistence exists in the package; unit tests read fixtures or temporary overlays without invoking fetchers.

data_operations.operation: Run a separate smoke-test collection path
data_operations.source: Default/optional overlay configuration, environment credentials, and optional source filters
data_operations.data_scope: Invokes real fetch scripts and merges their outputs; may write filtered configuration and fetched JSON to a test directory.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Same remote recipients as invoked fetchers; /tmp/tech-digest-test-*
data_operations.condition: test-pipeline.sh is explicitly invoked. Step and credential gates apply. Output directory is removed on success unless --keep is set; failures retain it.

potential_excess.data_scope: Official X context_annotations, author expansion, and expanded-user verified/public_metrics
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Official X tweet request/response boundary at api.x.com
potential_excess.condition: OfficialBackend fetches a monitored user's posts.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: The report requires post text, dates, links, and tweet engagement metrics; the parser does not consume context annotations or expanded user records.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Fetch enough tweet data for time filtering, reply exclusion, scoring, attribution, and the four displayed engagement metrics.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Remove context_annotations, expansions=author_id, and user.fields from this request. This narrows extra data in a required request rather than eliminating the request.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Keep created_at, public_metrics, referenced_tweets, post identifiers/text, and existing filtering and display behavior.

potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Python memory and an additional temporary PEM file before local openssl signing
potential_excess.purpose_basis: JWT signing requires access to the configured key; copying its contents into another file is an implementation choice.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Sign the constructed JWT with the configured private key.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Pass the original GH_APP_KEY_FILE path to openssl -sign, avoiding the Python key read and duplicate PEM persistence.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Preserve key-path validation, signing semantics, error handling, and the JWT exchange. The existing temporary copy is ordinarily deleted in finally.

potential_excess.data_scope: Repeated App credential access, signing, JWT disclosure, and installation-token creation
potential_excess.condition: Both release and trending steps run, GITHUB_TOKEN is absent, and App authentication succeeds in each process.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Both GitHub fetch paths need authentication, but they independently create installation tokens for the same configured installation.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Authenticate both required GitHub collection paths.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Resolve one short-lived installation token and share it only with the two GitHub steps. This removes a redundant token exchange, not either news-fetch operation.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Preserve authentication fallback, token validity, rate-limit behavior, independent command support, and release/trending coverage.

potential_excess.data_scope: All parent environment variables, including credentials unrelated to a particular step
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Every local fetch, merge, and enrichment subprocess launched by run_step
potential_excess.condition: Any pipeline step is launched with env=os.environ.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Fetchers need their own backend settings and credentials; merge and enrichment do not use the other services' API credentials.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Provide each child the environment needed for execution and its selected authentication path.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Construct per-step environment allowlists and omit unrelated API credentials, especially from merge and enrichment.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Retain required executable, filesystem, locale, TLS/proxy settings and component-specific backend/authentication variables. This finding concerns a local process boundary, not demonstrated remote transmission of the whole environment.

potential_excess.data_scope: Fetched/intermediate news records, enriched text, metadata/error tails, email HTML, PDF, and verbose PDF HTML
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Failed td-pipeline-* directories; final temporary JSON/.meta.json; /tmp/td-email.html; /tmp/td-digest.pdf; PDF HTML sidecars
potential_excess.condition: Merge failure bypasses run-directory cleanup; otherwise final handoff/delivery artifacts have no shown post-consumption deletion. Debug/reuse retention is explicitly selectable.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Temporary files support processing, delivery, and troubleshooting. The explicit 90-day archive requirement does not require these extra temporary copies to remain indefinitely.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Keep artifacts until their consumers, delivery attempts, and intended retries complete.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Clean generated run directories in finally and delete temporary delivery/handoff artifacts after consumption; apply bounded retention where troubleshooting is requested.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Preserve the required Markdown archive and its 90-day policy, caller-selected output retention, and explicit debug/reuse requirements.

potential_excess.data_scope: Expired or removed-source URL validators, handle/ID mappings, timestamps, and Brave quota records
potential_excess.condition: Cache files are reused over time; expired records are rejected for reuse but are not globally pruned from persisted dictionaries.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Cache freshness windows support efficient fetching; keeping records beyond those windows or after sources are removed is not needed for valid cache hits.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Reuse valid validators, account IDs, and quota state.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Evict expired records before saving and remove source-specific entries no longer configured.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Retain fresh entries for active sources and existing cache-bypass behavior; do not mistake freshness expiry for implemented file deletion.

potential_excess.data_scope: Old source names and timestamped success/failure history for sources absent from later updates
potential_excess.condition: A previously tracked source is omitted or disabled; pruning occurs only inside the loop over currently supplied sources.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: The health feature declares a seven-day history window, but inactive-source checks can remain beyond it.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Compute recent source failure rates and identify unhealthy sources.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Prune every stored source on each invocation and remove entries with no checks remaining in the window.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Keep active sources' seven-day checks and the existing minimum-check/failure-rate thresholds.

potential_excess.data_scope: Known nonfunctional campaign parameters such as utm_source and utm_medium in article URLs
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Article-origin requests during enrichment, digest recipients, and archived report links
potential_excess.condition: An original article link contains such parameters, as demonstrated by the RSS fixture. URL normalization strips queries only for duplicate comparison; original links remain available for fetching/display.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Reports require working source links and enrichment needs the article location; campaign attribution parameters need not accompany those required actions.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Preserve a working link to the same article.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Strip a narrow allowlist of known tracking parameters before fetch, display, and archival.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Keep functional query parameters, identifiers, and access requirements; do not remove all queries indiscriminately.

potential_excess.data_scope: Synthetic search request and associated Brave authentication
potential_excess.condition: A key needs uncached rate-limit probing and BRAVE_PLAN does not override detection.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Detecting rate limits supports collection, but the separate synthetic search returns no digest article.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Discover usable key/quota state and safe concurrency while performing configured searches.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Use the first required topic query as the probe and inspect its response headers before scheduling remaining requests.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Retain exhausted-key handling, rotation, cache behavior, conservative initial concurrency, and every required topic result. This removes a separate request rather than narrowing fields in a required search.

unknowns: Runtime workspace overrides, selected backends/credentials, delivery IDs/addresses, archive contents, and actual invocations are unavailable. Operations are therefore conditional; concrete user-specific destinations cannot be determined.

Provider-side logging, retention, secondary use, onward disclosure, and deletion are undocumented. The source does not establish those behaviors for news APIs, feed/article servers, or delivery providers.

gh credential-store internals, mail transport configuration, gog behavior, message-tool handling, weasyprint internals, and host log retention are outside the supplied implementation. Local handoffs do not establish additional remote recipients.

Without usable search credentials, fetch-web.py generates local web_search instructions; whether the agent executes them, and which provider receives the queries, is unresolved (scripts/fetch-web.py:447-471).
The agent interprets prompt instructions for report generation, delivery, archival, and 90-day deletion; execution or successful deletion cannot be verified from source.

summarize-merged.py does not print full_text or trending-specific fields and limits items per topic. How the agent obtains those fields and all required releases beyond that overview is unresolved; enrichment is explicitly intended for richer summaries, so its use cannot simply be classified as unnecessary (references/digest-prompt.md:60-67,92-111; scripts/summarize-merged.py:35-81).

Email routing instructions conflict: the main prompt uses send-email.py, while email/PDF templates describe gog or mail. The actual route chosen by an interpreting agent is unresolved (references/digest-prompt.md:133-148; references/templates/email.md:5-13; references/templates/pdf.md:65-74).
